explanations: terra: The warning makes no difference to those who kafarū, and they will not believe; this identifies the resistant stance upon which the eye-cover descends in 2:7.

luna: The same cover word named for Ghashiya appears as a veil over disbelievers' sight (غِشَاوَةٌ) alongside great punishment; it connects covering the truth with covered perception. | terra: A غشاوة lies over the disbelievers' sight after their resistance to warning; the section's claim that covering truth ends in covered perception is stated bodily here.
terra: God makes earth a bed and sky a structure, then sends rain and brings out fruit; an overhead cover, the ground below, and productive growth form a life-giving enclosure.
terra: God shades Israel with clouds and sends food, so the descending overhead cover gives provision and safety rather than punishment.

luna: The speakers describe their own hearts as wrapped (قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ); their claimed closedness gives another form of the section's inner-cover image around refusal. | terra: The rejecters say their hearts are wrapped, while the ayah attributes their exclusion to kufr; the claimed inner cover functions as a defense against revealed truth.
luna: Those who hide clear proofs and guidance after its disclosure enact the section's dictionary branch of disbelief as covering what is true.
terra: The faithful prayer asks for good in both lives and protection from the punishment of Fire, repeating the section's protective stance in a compact supplication.
terra: The warning asks whether people await God's decisive coming amid canopies of cloud; an overhead covering accompanies the arrival of settled judgment.
luna: A single grain produces seven ears and multiplies its yield; read beside the section's farmer-covering-seed branch, it gives a concrete image of what hidden growth under soil can become.
terra: A rainstorm strips the dust from a smooth rock and leaves it bare, making ostentatious giving yield nothing; the verse ends with the people who kafarū unguided.

luna: A parable describes a Garden on high ground that yields double produce after heavy rain; the high, fruitful Jannah connects the section's elevated Garden to growth under a covering soil. | terra: Sincere spending is like a high garden whose yield doubles under rain; this is the fruitful cultivated cover set against the fire-struck garden in the following ayah.

luna: A garden of date palms and grapes is struck by a fiery whirlwind and burned; this is a concrete reversal of the section's Garden as a shelter from scorching punishment. | terra: A fruitful palm-and-grape garden is struck by a fiery whirlwind when its elderly owner is most vulnerable; cultivated cover, provision, and protection vanish together.
luna: The verse asks why people clothe truth in falsehood and conceal it while knowing (تَلْبِسُونَ الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ); it spells out the section's dictionary claim that kufr covers truth.

luna: On the Day some faces turn white and others black (تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ); the split face-scene contrasts with the two kinds of faces in the section. | terra: The Day when some faces whiten and others blacken ties darkened faces to disbelief after faith and to tasting punishment.

luna: The white-faced people are in God's mercy and remain there; this gives the section's pleasant garden-side faces a specific judgment-day counterpart to the darkened faces of the previous verse. | terra: The whitened faces remain in God's mercy, forming the protected facial counterpart to the punished faces in the preceding ayah.
terra: Neither wealth nor children avail those who kafarū against God, and they belong to the Fire; this identifies the people whose cultivated wealth is destroyed in the next ayah's comparison.
terra: The rejecters' spending is likened to an icy wind that strikes and destroys a people's crop; their moral covering yields a visibly ruined planting.

luna: The section's covering root is used when drowsiness comes over a group (يَغْشَى طَائِفَةً مِّنكُمْ نُعَاسًا); it gives the inward, consciousness-covering side of the image in a scene of fear. | terra: After distress, security is sent down as drowsiness يغشى a group; the same inwardly reaching cover that can overwhelm understanding here calms and protects it.
terra: Those reflecting on creation ask their Lord to protect them from the punishment of Fire; cosmic perception culminates in the same request for a true shield.

luna: The Garden promised to believers includes deep shade (ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا); it states the sheltering quality of the section's reward in another direct Garden scene. | terra: Those who believe enter gardens and are admitted into ظلا ظليلا, abundant deep shade; the Garden's reward is explicitly figured as a protective covering.
terra: Their hearts are sealed because of covenant-breaking and kufr, so belief scarcely enters; covering truth is again answered by a closed faculty.

luna: The section's H-M-Y dictionary branch describes protected grazing land; the verse names the Hām as an animal treated as reserved by custom. If that name carries the same protection sense, it contrasts human-declared protection with the section's protection from scorching punishment. | terra: God did not institute the protected livestock called hām, but disbelievers fabricated the rule; the related h-m-y protection term exposes a human-made sanctuary joined to kufr.

luna: The verse says coverings lie over disbelievers' hearts so they cannot understand (أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ); it gives a cognitive counterpart to the section's dictionary image of an event covering understanding. | terra: Some listen while covers are placed over their hearts so they do not understand and heaviness is in their ears; sensory access remains while meaning is hidden.
terra: God can send punishment from above or from beneath people's feet, or confound them in hostile groups; the first two possibilities anticipate the total vertical enclosure of 29:55.

luna: When night covers Abraham (جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ), the section's named garden root appears in another branch with the same concealing image; the star's setting then makes the cover part of Abraham's rejection of transient objects. | terra: Night جنّ over Abraham and hid the field of sight; this is the second root in the section's three-root night image and makes j-n-n's concealment sensory and concrete.

luna: After their nakedness appears, Adam and his spouse fasten leaves of the Garden over themselves (مِن وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ); here garden growth literally conceals exposed bodies, a distinct counterpart to trees covering the ground.

luna: The verse says clothing is given to cover people's nakedness (لِبَاسًا يُوَارِي سَوْآتِكُمْ); it extends the section's ordinary covering image from a saddle cloth to bodily concealment. | terra: Clothing is sent down to cover nakedness and as adornment, while the garment of reverence is better; bodily and inward coverings are distinguished as genuine gifts.
terra: Satan stripped the first parents of their clothing to expose what had been hidden; the verse makes loss of cover an exposure produced through deception.

luna: The section's Ghashiya covering has a matching form in the coverings over Hell's people (غَوَاشٍ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ), with bedding below and covers above turning enclosure into torment. | terra: Hell is a bed beneath its people and غواش above them, giving the punitive cover both a lower support and upper layers exactly as the section's enclosure requires.

luna: God covers the day with night (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ); this makes the section's night-as-cover image cosmic and recurrent. | terra: God makes night يغشي the day, pursuing it swiftly; the verse gives the Ghashiya root a recurrent cosmic motion in which one expanse is laid over another.

luna: Moses falls stunned when the mountain crumbles at the manifestation of his Lord; this is a concrete instance of the inward collapse that the section's fainting dictionary branch places beside an outer cover.
terra: God again shades the tribes with clouds while providing manna, quails, and water; the repeated canopy is a life-giving cover from above.
terra: The mountain is raised over the people as though it were a canopy and they think it will fall; an overhead cover becomes covenantal terror rather than shelter.

terra: The verb تغشاها euphemistically describes one spouse covering the other before pregnancy begins; this may illuminate a life-producing bodily use of the root beside Ghashiya's destructive cover.

luna: Sleep comes over the believers as security (النُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً) before rain strengthens them; it shows a covering of consciousness that protects, unlike the overpowering cover of punishment. | terra: Drowsiness يغشيكم as security from God before purifying rain; a descending cover becomes reassurance rather than the terror carried by Ghashiya.

luna: This verse says neither dust nor humiliation covers the good-doers' faces and names them as Garden companions; its own contribution is the uncovered, protected face opposite the darkened face in 10:27 and the section's opposed outcomes. | terra: For those who do good, neither darkness nor humiliation covers their faces; this explicit protected face is the immediate boundary against the night-covered faces of 10:27.

luna: The source section names Ghashiya as an encompassing cover; here dark pieces of night cover wrongdoers' faces (أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ), turning night-cover into punishment opposite the garden's shelter. | terra: Dark pieces of night seem to have been أُغْشِيَتْ over the evildoers' faces; the ayah turns the section's night-as-cover into the visible mark of judgment.
luna: The section names the Ghashiya covering root; here people cover themselves with their garments to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and reveal, joining an outer cover to inward secrecy.

luna: Noah's son expects a mountain to shield him from the flood, but the wave comes between them; this reverses the section's assurance that God protects the garden people from overwhelming punishment. | terra: Noah's son seeks a mountain to protect him from the water, but no protector exists from God's command and the wave intervenes; imagined shelter fails inside an overwhelming flood.
terra: The Prophet is told that most people will not believe despite his eagerness; this supplies the resistant audience from which the warning question of 12:107 arises.

luna: The section says the source word غاشية names the Hour as a cover that comes over creation; Yusuf's warning asks whether people feel safe from غاشية من عذاب الله, making the same arriving cover an explicit punishment. | terra: The ayah itself names a غاشية that may come from God's punishment, joining the section's arriving cover, its punitive scope, and its warning question in one formulation.

luna: The same covering verb describes night covering day (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ), repeating the section's physical image in a passage about God's signs. | terra: Night يغشي the day amid the ordering of earth, rivers, and fruits; the recurring cover belongs to the same created world in which garden growth can shelter the ground.
terra: The disbelievers have punishment in this life, harsher punishment in the next, and no wāqī from God; the protective verb underlying the section's shield is explicitly denied.

luna: The promised garden's food and shade endure (أُكُلُهَا دَائِمٌ وَظِلُّهَا); this gives the section's sheltering garden a lasting quality against transient coverings. | terra: The promised Garden has lasting fruit and lasting shade, while the rejecters' end is fire; enduring tree-cover and punitive exposure are placed at the passage's boundary.
terra: The deeds of those who kafarū are ashes scattered by a violent wind, leaving them unable to retain anything earned; truth-covering produces no lasting growth or shelter.
terra: A good word is like a good tree with a firm root and branches in the sky; truth becomes the living upward-grown cover implicit in the section's garden.
terra: The good tree gives fruit in every season by its Lord's leave; the verse supplies what can grow from a sound planting rather than from covering truth.
terra: An evil word is like an uprooted tree with no stability; it is the specific reversal of the section's fruitful farmer-cover, producing no enduring shelter.
terra: The criminals are seen bound together in chains before pitch clothes and face-covering fire are described; their bodily enclosure begins before the fiery cover lands.

luna: The section's Ghashiya root becomes bodily visible when fire covers the faces of people whose clothing is tar; it shows how an outer covering can overwhelm the face. | terra: Fire تغشى the criminals' faces while their pitch garments surround their bodies; this is the section's crushing outer cover landing first on the exposed front of the person.

luna: God gives garments that protect people from heat and from violence (سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ); this names the protective work that the section's garden-cover performs, against its searing fire. | terra: God makes shade, mountain shelters, and garments that protect from heat and violence; these are the creaturely covers whose presence defines by contrast what the punished person has lost.
terra: Those who prefer the nearer life over the Hereafter are identified as disbelievers whom God does not guide, establishing the choice behind the sealing described next.
terra: God seals their hearts, hearing, and sight, leaving them heedless; the prior preference and kufr become a cover over every receiving faculty.
luna: The night is made dark and the day luminous as paired signs; the verse develops the boundary between obscuring night and visible day that the section traces through night-cover images.

luna: A hidden barrier is placed between the Prophet and those who do not believe in the Hereafter when the Quran is recited; it is another specific veil on reception, distinct from the heart-cover in the section. | terra: Recitation places a hidden veil between the Prophet and those who do not believe in the Hereafter; revealed truth itself marks the boundary their refusal cannot cross.

luna: Coverings over hearts prevent understanding and heaviness affects the ears; this closely matches the section's movement from an outer cover to perception and thought. | terra: God places أكنة over their hearts lest they understand and heaviness in their ears, after which they turn their backs; the cover works inward upon comprehension.

luna: The fire's enclosure surrounds those who do wrong (سُرَادِقُهَا); it supplies another explicit image of punishment hemming people in, like the section's covering calamity. | terra: The wrongdoers are surrounded by a fire whose enclosing walls are described like a pavilion; the architectural form of shelter becomes the material of punishment.
terra: The believers inhabit gardens, wear garments, and recline on couches, supplying the sheltering counterpart to the fire-pavilion that encloses the wrongdoers in 18:29.
terra: Two grape gardens are surrounded with palms and set around crops; the arrangement makes the etymological Garden visible as earth enclosed beneath cultivated growth.

luna: A garden owner says he does not think his orchard will ever perish; beside the section's hidden, lasting Garden, his visible garden exposes the false security of treating an earthly cover as permanent. | terra: The owner enters his garden while wronging himself and declares that it will never perish; he mistakes a created cover for permanent security.
terra: He doubts the Hour and assumes an even better return, exposing the denial that makes his confidence in the garden spiritually barren.
terra: His companion asks أَكَفَرْتَ in the middle of the garden dispute; kufr is named at the point where created protection is being treated as self-sufficient.
terra: The companion warns that a reckoning may turn the garden into a barren slippery tract; tree-cover and fertile soil can be removed together.
terra: Its water may sink beyond recovery, showing how the hidden support of the cultivated cover can be withdrawn.

luna: The owner's fruit is encompassed by ruin (أُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ); the failed orchard contrasts with the section's garden as a protecting and hidden reward. | terra: The owner's fruit is encompassed and he wrings his hands over collapsed trellises; the garden that once enclosed the ground is itself enclosed by ruin.
terra: After the garden's ruin, its owner has no party to help him apart from God and cannot defend himself; garden-cover and human protection disappear together.
terra: After the garden owner proves unable to protect himself, the passage says all protective authority belongs to God; this identifies the source of the only cover that endures.
terra: The one who turns away after reminder has covers placed over the heart and heaviness in the ears; deliberate truth-covering becomes incapacity to understand it.
terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn finds a people for whom God made no ستر against the sun; this is the section's dictionary picture of the uncovered person with no barrier toward the sky.
terra: Their eyes had been under a غطاء from God's reminder and they could not hear; the ayah directly joins chosen inattention to a cover over perception.
terra: The promised Gardens of Eden are بالغيب, belonging to the unseen while God's promise will arrive; hidden reward and eventual arrival are joined in one ayah.
terra: What covered Pharaoh's people from the sea غشيهم; the deliberately repeated covering verb makes annihilating water another concrete form of the all-enveloping event.

luna: On the Day, faces are humbled before the Living and Sustaining One (وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ); it closely parallels the section's low, subdued faces. | terra: Faces are humbled before the Living, Self-Sustaining Lord, and the bearer of wrongdoing fails; this directly repeats the eschatological face lowered by the event.
terra: God makes the sky a protected roof, yet people turn from its signs; the normal overhead expanse is a preserved shelter rather than the descending punitive cover.
terra: The rejecters cannot keep the Fire from their faces or backs and receive no help; punishment reaches exposed fronts and rears when no protective covering remains.

luna: God teaches David to make armor that protects people from their violence; this is a concrete shield-like covering and gives the section's protective Garden cover a bodily counterpart. | terra: God teaches David the making of armor to protect people from their violence; the material coat performs the shielding work named in the section's definition of جنة.
terra: The command to fear the Lord is grounded in the tremendous convulsion of the Hour; this supplies the creation-wide terror by which the section says Ghashiya covers its subjects.
terra: The quake makes nursing mothers forget, pregnancies end, and people look intoxicated although they are not; an outer event has penetrated awareness and bodily control.
luna: The condemned are given garments of fire (ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارٍ); the image reverses an ordinary covering that conceals or protects into one that torments.
terra: God restrains the sky from falling upon earth except by His permission; the verse identifies divine mercy in holding the overhead cover safely in place.

luna: Their hearts are in a covering of heedlessness about the revelation (فِي غَمْرَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا); this is a distinct word for a mind submerged from what it should perceive, like the section's fainting branch.

luna: Fire sears their faces (تَلْفَحُ وُجُوهَهُمُ النَّارُ), a direct bodily counterpart to faces covered by fire in the section, with the verse adding their grimace. | terra: Fire scorches their faces until their mouths contort, giving another direct staging of punishment reaching the exposed front of the person.
terra: The deeds of those who kafarū are a mirage that leaves the thirsty finder with nothing; this supplies the fruitless truth-cover immediately before the layered darkness of 24:40.

luna: The parable layers darkness in a deep sea, with wave over wave and cloud above, until a person can scarcely see a hand; it gives a specific, layered cover that reaches sight. | terra: A wave يغشاه, above it another wave, and above that a cloud, until layered darkness prevents sight; this concretely joins surrounding cover, descent from above, and blinded perception.
terra: God extends the shadow and appoints the sun as its guide; the relation between overhead light and sheltering cover is presented as a deliberately governed sign.
terra: God gradually draws the shadow back, making protective cover visibly removable rather than self-sustaining.
luna: Night is made a garment and sleep a rest (اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَالنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا), joining the section's covering night to the inward quiet of sleep before the day resumes.
terra: The deniers demand that pieces of sky be dropped on them; their challenge supplies the overhead fall answered by the punitive canopy in 26:189.

luna: The people of Shu'ayb receive the punishment of the Day of the Shade (عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ); a shade becomes an enveloping punishment rather than the garden's refuge. | terra: The punishment of the Day of the Canopy seizes the deniers; a cloud-like overhead cover, normally capable of shade, becomes the named vehicle of a terrible punishment.
terra: Before the cover closes from above and below, Hell is already said to encompass the kāfirīn; encirclement and truth-covering meet in the lead-in to 29:55.

luna: The same covering verb named in the section describes punishment closing over people from above and beneath their feet; it completes the all-around movement of the Ghashiya image. | terra: Punishment يغشاهم from above them and from beneath their feet; it realizes the section's cover as total enclosure rather than a sheet resting only overhead.

luna: The verse says waves cover people like canopies (غَشِيَهُم مَوْجٌ كَالظُّلَلِ); the cover is lethal danger, and so sharpens the section's distinction between an oppressive and a protecting cover. | terra: A wave يغشيهم like canopies, prompting sincere prayer, yet rescue is followed by denial; the ayah binds an overwhelming cover to the exposure and return of kufr.

luna: The section's dictionary describes Paradise as a reward hidden from people today; this verse says no soul knows what has been hidden for them as delight (أُخْفِيَ لَهُم), making that concealment part of the promised garden's appeal. | terra: No soul knows what comfort has been hidden for it as reward; this directly states the section's claim that the Garden is a recompense still covered from present perception.
terra: Enemies come from above and below, eyes swerve, and hearts reach throats; surrounding danger penetrates sight and mind just as the section's outer cover works inward.
terra: Fear makes the hypocrites' eyes roll like one يُغشى عليه من الموت; an external danger reaches consciousness and overwhelms it, enacting the section's inward extension of the cover.
terra: Faces are turned about in the Fire while their owners regret disobedience; the exposed front of the person remains the visible site on which punishment works.
terra: Those who disbelieve are asked to consider earth below and sky above, either of which could become punishment; their apparently stable enclosure depends wholly on God.
terra: Saba has two gardens on the right and left, provision within a good land; the ayah stages inhabited life between productive covers before the people's turning away.
terra: When the people turn away, the flood of the dam replaces their two gardens with bitter, sparse growth; a sheltering productive landscape is stripped through refusal.
terra: The exchange of gardens is called repayment for their kufr, and the verse asks whether anyone but the deeply ungrateful is so repaid; truth-covering yields a devastated cover.
terra: Shackles reach the rejecters' chins and constrain their heads immediately before barriers and covered sight are described; bodily enclosure precedes perceptual enclosure.
terra: Barriers enclose the rejecters before and behind, then God says فأغشيناهم so they do not see; an outer enclosure becomes an inward failure of sight.

luna: God strips the day from the night (نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ), leaving people in darkness; this gives the night-cover image its opposite motion, light removed rather than night laid over it. | terra: God strips daylight from night and people are left in darkness; visibility appears as a removable layer, complementing the section's picture of night laid over the seen world.

luna: The Garden's people and spouses rest in shade; this makes the Garden a place of shelter, extending the section's image of a covering that protects. | terra: The companions of the Garden and their spouses are occupied joyfully في ظلال on couches; Paradise is staged as life beneath sheltering shade.

luna: The verse pictures God wrapping night over day and day over night (يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ); it makes the section's covering motion a recurring cosmic turning. | terra: God wraps night over day and day over night, using a nonlexical wrapping image for the same alternating cosmic cover heard in the section's night vocabulary.

luna: Fire canopies stand above and below Hell's people; this gives the section's crushing cover a two-sided counterpart to the garden's protective growth. | terra: The damned have canopies of fire above and canopies beneath, and God uses this scene to make His servants fear; the enclosing cover has become the thing feared.
terra: A person has only his face with which to ward the evil punishment on Resurrection; the first surface struck has become a last, inadequate shield because every other cover is gone.

luna: On the Day the faces of those who lied about God are blackened; this ties a disbelieving stance to the darkened face that contrasts with the section's garden faces. | terra: Those who lied against God are seen on Resurrection with blackened faces; judgment makes the prior inward falsification visible on the face.
luna: The section's dictionary gives fainting as an inward effect of being covered; here the trumpet makes those in the heavens and earth fall stunned, then they rise at the next blast.

luna: The angels ask God to protect believers from Hell and admit them to gardens; this joins the section's two covers in one passage, protection from torment and entry into the garden. | terra: The throne-bearing angels ask forgiveness for the repentant and ask God to protect them from the punishment of Hell, using protective prayer against the consuming cover.
terra: The angels ask that the believers and their righteous families enter the promised Gardens of Eden; Garden and family are held inside the prayer for protection.
terra: They ask God to protect them from evils, and say whoever is protected that Day has received mercy; protection is defined at the exact temporal boundary of judgment.
luna: When all come forth, nothing about them is hidden from God; this gives the exposed opposite of the section's enveloping and concealing covers.
terra: On the Day of turning away, people have no protector from God; flight exposes the person for whom every sheltering relation has closed.

luna: The speakers say their hearts are in coverings from the message (قُلُوبُنَا فِي أَكِنَّةٍ); this makes cognitive concealment an expressed response to truth. | terra: The rejecters claim their hearts are in أكنة, their ears bear heaviness, and a veil stands between them and the messenger; resistance is described as layered insulation from truth.

luna: Wrongdoers are brought near the Fire, humiliated and watching furtively; this extends the section's humbled face into an exposed, fearful posture before punishment. | terra: The wrongdoers are presented to the Fire خاشعين من الذل and look furtively; the section's humbled face becomes a whole posture under punishment.
terra: People are told to answer before a day with no refuge from God arrives; the warning stance is sharpened by the announced absence of protective cover.
luna: God's speech can come from behind a veil (مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ); this is a distinct, non-punitive use of concealment that marks a boundary of perception beside the section's enveloping cover.
terra: The command is to watch for the day when the sky brings visible smoke; this ayah supplies the descending object that covers people in the following ayah.

luna: The section's covering root is used of the smoke that covers people (يَغْشَى النَّاسَ); smoke becomes another enveloping form of punishment. | terra: The smoke يغشى الناس and is immediately identified as painful punishment, making the Ghashiya movement a palpable cover that reaches people from the sky.
luna: After the smoke covers people in 44:11, they plead for the punishment to be removed; this verse contributes the afflicted people's response to that specific cover.
luna: The God-fearing are placed in a secure abode (مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ), the refuge side of the same surah whose smoke covers people in 44:11; it contrasts safety with an enveloping punishment.

luna: God protects the Garden people from the punishment of Hell (وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ); it repeats the section's defining contrast between protection and punishment. | terra: The Garden people taste no further death and God protects them from the punishment of Hell; hidden reward and deliverance from the crushing cover coincide.

luna: God places a covering over the sight of one who follows desire as a god, alongside a seal on hearing and heart; this joins outer sight and inward judgment as the section's cover image does. | terra: The self-deifying follower of desire has hearing and heart sealed and a غشاوة placed over sight; this shows truth-covering as a cover that reaches the faculties of understanding.
luna: A cloud approaches and is mistaken for rain, but proves to be a wind carrying painful punishment; the apparent covering from the sky becomes a threat rather than provision.
terra: Those with diseased hearts look like one يُغشى عليه من الموت when fighting is disclosed; this is the source section's secondary sense of an event covering understanding into a faint.

luna: The verse compares the believers to a crop that sends out shoots and thickens, delighting its sowers; it shows the growth possible beneath a covering soil, which the section contrasts with covering truth so nothing grows. | terra: Believers are pictured as a crop that emerges, thickens, and delights its sowers while enraging the disbelievers; the ayah sets fruitful cultivation directly against kufr.

luna: After saying the person was heedless, God removes his covering (غِطَاءَكَ) and his sight becomes sharp; this reverses the section's cover that reaches inward to understanding. | terra: At judgment the heedless person's غطاء is removed and sight becomes sharp; the earlier perceptual cover vanishes precisely when the overwhelming reality can no longer be hidden.
terra: The Garden is brought near to the God-fearing after having been an unseen promise; what was covered from present perception becomes immediate.
terra: The promised Garden belongs to one who feared the Merciful in the unseen and came with a returning heart; hidden reward answers hidden fear.
terra: The God-fearing are in gardens and bliss immediately before their protection from Hell is named, making the positive cover the setting of their rescue.
terra: The Garden people rejoice because their Lord protected them from the punishment of the Blaze; it is a second direct formulation of the protective claim later voiced in 52:27.
terra: The people of the Garden turn toward one another and ask, beginning the remembered family conversation that the section invokes before their statement of protection.
terra: They say that formerly, among their family, they lived in fear; this supplies the precise earlier stance from which the Garden's protective cover is understood.

luna: The garden people say God protected them from the scorching torment (وَوَقَانَا عَذَابَ السَّمُومِ); this is the section's clearest example of the garden's covering as a shield against heat. | terra: They say God favored them and وقانا the scorching punishment; the protecting verb is exactly the verb used in the section's dictionary definition of a shield.
terra: They recall that they used to call upon God and name Him gracious and merciful; their former appeal completes the passage's movement from fear to bestowed protection.
terra: Even if the deniers saw a piece of sky falling, they would call it a massed cloud; what appears capable of shade conceals the punishment they refuse to recognize.
luna: The Quran names the garden at the Lote Tree as the Garden of Refuge (جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَىٰ); this brings out the sheltering sense of the section's garden and shield dictionary branches.
terra: God covered the overturned settlements with what covered them, فغشاها ما غشى; the unspecified cover conveys the same overwhelming completeness carried by the name Ghashiya.
luna: The disbelievers emerge from graves with humbled eyes (خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ); it gives another judgment-day counterpart to the section's humbled faces.
terra: The two promised gardens possess spreading branches, giving a concise visual form to the tree-grown cover heard in the name jannah.

luna: The Garden of the right hand has extended shade (وَظِلٍّ مَّمْدُودٍ); this is a direct tree-covering refuge that gives the section's garden shelter a concrete form. | terra: Extended shade is one of the concrete provisions for the companions of the right; the Garden's covering is spacious, sustaining, and non-crushing.
luna: The people of the left are in scorching wind and boiling water; this establishes the heat against which the section's protected garden offers shelter.

luna: Their shade is black smoke (ظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ), an enclosing shade that carries torment rather than protection. | terra: The companions of the left are in a shade of black smoke, turning the Garden's sheltering tree-cover into a suffocating imitation of shade.

luna: The verse says that this shade is neither cool nor generous (لَا بَارِدٍ وَلَا كَرِيمٍ); it explicitly denies the sheltering benefit the section hears in the garden's cover. | terra: That smoke-shade is neither cool nor generous; the ayah states exactly why this cover fails the protective work performed by Garden shade.
terra: A wall with a gate separates mercy on its inner side from punishment outside; one structure becomes the exact boundary between protective enclosure and punitive exposure.

luna: The section's dictionary labels the farmer as a coverer of seed; this verse uses الكُفَّار for cultivators whose rain-grown plant first delights, then dries and crumbles, making the seed-covering branch and its transience visible. | terra: The rain-grown crop delights the الكفار in the verse's farmer sense, then yellows and crumbles before final punishment or forgiveness; productive covering and final outcomes meet explicitly.

luna: The section's J-N-N dictionary branch defines a shield as something that protects; this verse says people use their oaths as a shield while turning others from God's way, a deceptive protection unlike the Garden's refuge. | terra: The hypocrites take their oaths as جنة, a shield, to obstruct God's path, but receive humiliating punishment; a self-made verbal cover cannot provide the protection its root promises.

luna: The same shield phrase recurs: the hypocrites take their oaths as a shield and then turn away from God's path; it repeats the section's protective J-N-N branch in a false, concealing use. | terra: Their oaths are used as جنة while they turn others from God's path; the shield sense of the Garden root is exposed here as a deceptive cover for corrupt action.
terra: Because they believed and then kafarū, their hearts were sealed so they do not understand; the act of covering truth results in a closed faculty.
terra: Believers are commanded to protect themselves and their families from a Fire fueled by people and stones; this turns remembered family fear into an urgent present duty.
terra: When the promised punishment draws near, the faces of those who kafarū become distressed; the truth-coverer's face registers the arrival of what had been denied.
terra: The garden owners are tested as earlier owners were when they swore to harvest at dawn; a garden becomes the setting in which concealed intention is exposed.
terra: A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while its owners sleep; punishment overtakes the protected plot from outside their awareness.
terra: By morning the garden is like a dark, harvested tract; the living cover has become visually indistinguishable from night or barrenness.
terra: The chastened garden owners hope their Lord will replace the lost plot with a better one; ruined cover becomes an occasion to seek a newly bestowed garden.
terra: The ruined garden episode is identified as punishment, with the Hereafter's punishment greater; loss of cultivated cover becomes a near image of final exposure.
terra: Their eyes are humbled and humiliation ترهقهم, covering them after they refused the summons while able; moral refusal becomes an enveloping public abasement.
luna: On that Day nothing about the people is hidden (لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ); it marks the boundary where every worldly concealment is removed.

luna: People hurry out from their graves on the Day like racers to a marker; this gives the movement into the humbled-eye and overwhelming humiliation scene in 70:44, paralleling the section's judgment-day gathering.

luna: Their eyes are humbled and humiliation overwhelms them (تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ); this joins the lowered face to an affliction that covers, as in the section's judgment scene. | terra: They rush from the graves with lowered eyes while humiliation ترهقهم; the promised Day arrives as the cover of abasement already pictured on the faces of surah 88.
terra: When the human asks where to flee on that Day, the answer is that there is no refuge; the overwhelming event removes every possible outer shelter.
luna: Some faces on that Day are radiant (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ); they parallel the section's pleasant faces against the humbled ones.
luna: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord (إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ); their orientation adds a distinct posture to the bright side of the section's face-scene.

luna: Other faces are gloomy (وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَاسِرَةٌ), the opposite bodily state to the section's pleasant faces. | terra: Some faces on that Day are gloomy, furnishing another direct facial condition under the approaching event.

luna: Those gloomy faces expect a calamity to break them; this names the inward dread behind the lowered and burdened faces of the section. | terra: Those faces expect a back-breaking calamity, so their visible gloom registers conscious anticipation of the crushing cover.
terra: God protects the righteous from the evil of that Day and meets them with radiance and joy; protection from the overwhelming event appears visibly on their faces.
terra: Their patience is repaid with a Garden and silk, giving the positive cover that follows God's protection from the Day in the preceding ayah.

luna: The garden's people rest in shade without seeing sun or bitter cold; its protection from exposure makes concrete the section's garden as a covering refuge. | terra: Reclining in the Garden, they encounter neither sun nor bitter cold; the reward removes the exposed person's direct vulnerability to the sky.

luna: The Garden's shade hangs close over its people and its fruit is brought low; this develops the section's protective tree-cover as an enclosing, accessible shelter. | terra: The Garden's shades hang close over them and its fruit is lowered within reach; trees form the sheltering cover that the section hears in the name jannah.

luna: The condemned are sent toward a shade with three branches (ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلَاثِ شُعَبٍ); the following verse denies that it shades or protects, reversing the section's garden-cover. | terra: The rejecters are ordered toward a three-branched shadow; the command offers the outward form of shelter as part of punishment.

luna: This verse says that shade does not protect from the flame (لَا ظَلِيلٍ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ); it directly contrasts the source section's shield-like garden. | terra: The three-branched shadow neither shades nor protects from flame; it is the section's shield definition negated inside a counterfeit cover.
terra: The God-fearing are amid shades and springs, directly answering the false fire-shadow assigned to the rejecters earlier in the same surah.
luna: Night is made a garment (اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا), a direct clothing image for the cover the section traces through night and Ghashiya.
terra: Dense, entwined gardens are among God's provisions, making the Garden's name visually apt through foliage that covers and encloses the ground.
luna: Hearts tremble on that Day; this supplies the inward fear behind the humbled eyes in the next verse and the section's externally visible submission.
luna: Eyes are humbled (أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ), paralleling the section's humbled faces; the preceding verse 79:8 contributes the fear within that becomes visible in the eyes.
luna: God darkens the night and brings out the morning light; this gives the covered night a visible boundary, when the light that it hid returns.
terra: The arrival of the greatest overwhelming calamity supplies a close nonlexical name for the all-surpassing event that Ghashiya makes perceptible as a cover.
luna: Some faces on that Day are bright (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّسْفِرَةٌ); this begins a face-by-face contrast that clarifies the section's divided outcomes.
luna: Those bright faces are laughing and rejoicing; their visible ease contrasts with the humbled faces in the section.

luna: Other faces have dust upon them (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ); the material covering makes the section's face-cover image concrete. | terra: Dust lies on faces on that Day, placing a material-looking cover on the very surface the section identifies as the first place struck.

luna: Darkness overwhelms those faces (تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ); this completes the covered, degraded face opposite the bright face in 80:38. | terra: Darkness ترهق those faces, adding a second oppressive layer over the dust and closely repeating the section's night-covered face.

luna: The verse identifies the dust-covered faces in 80:40–41 as the disbelieving wicked (الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ); it links the covered face to the section's K-F-R branch of truth-covering. | terra: The dust-darkened faces are identified as those who kafarū and transgressed; the passage joins the truth-coverer to the face that has itself become covered.

luna: What they earned has rusted over their hearts (رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم); this gives a concrete image of wrongdoing accumulating as an inner veil. | terra: What people earned has rusted over their hearts; the nonlexical heart-cover shows how repeated acts can conceal truth from within before the final outer cover arrives.

luna: The wrongdoers are screened from their Lord on that Day (لَمَحْجُوبُونَ); its own contribution is exclusion by a veil, opposite the Garden's protecting cover, after the prior verse describes hearts obscured by their deeds. | terra: After their deeds rust over their hearts, they are veiled from their Lord on that Day; the inward cover of 83:14 reaches its final relational consequence.
luna: The Day secrets are tested and brought out (تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ); it shows inward concealment opening, a boundary to the section's cover over understanding.
luna: The day is sworn by when it displays; this verse supplies the daylight boundary to the night-cover in 91:4, and its own contribution is the revealed side of that pair.

luna: The oath by night uses the section's covering verb (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا); it is a direct occurrence of the night-cover image that the section traces across roots. | terra: Night is sworn by when it يغشاها, covering the sun; this repeated night image clarifies covering as the withdrawal of visibility rather than mere contact.

luna: The oath names night when it covers (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ), the same night-cover image the section hears in Ghashiya and in its other root branches. | terra: The oath by night when it يغشى supplies the section's explicit natural model: darkness arrives from outside and covers what had been visible.
luna: The day is sworn by when it appears (وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ); it completes the night-covering in 92:1 with the image's opposite, daylight made manifest.
terra: The abyss is identified as نار حامية, repeating the exact fire description outside surah 88 and keeping the root's burning sense beside the section's protected-place dictionary branch.
luna: The fire is described as reaching the hearts (تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ); this is a specific inner reach for the section's image of an outer cover working inward to thought.
luna: The Fire is closed over its people (مُّؤْصَدَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ); it is a direct enclosing punishment, the oppressive counterpart to the Garden's protective covering.
luna: The enclosing fire is held by extended pillars; this verse gives the physical form of the closure stated in 104:8, adding how its covering is fixed around them.
